title: Judge Says U.S. Must Help Bring Man Home
summary:
A U.S. judge ordered the Department of Homeland Security to help bring Ahmed Soliman back to the United States.

Soliman lived in Arizona. He came to the U.S. as a young child. He was sent earlier this year to Equatorial Guinea. That country was not his home country. This kind of move is called a third-country deportation.

Reuters says he was sent in April before some of his court cases were finished. Judge John C. Hinderaker said the government must help free him from custody there and arrange travel papers for his return.

Homeland Security did not comment right away. Equatorial Guinea also did not answer questions, Reuters said. The case is about due process—the idea that people should get fair hearings.
why_it_matters: Court cases like this show kids that rules about fair hearings can protect people.
